Twenty-year backtest: strategy S1

Top 4 unexplained S&P 500 losers each day (skip earnings that day or the evening before, an 8%+ opening gap, and reports due in the next 10 days), bought at the next open, $1,000 each, sold by a 12% trailing stop; at most 24 positions, 2 new buys per sector per day, 10-day cool-off. $24,000 account; idle cash earns T-bills. 2005-01-04 to 2026-10-30. Rules and pass marks were committed before the run.

Verdict

S1 FAILED on the never-tested period (2005-01-04 to Oct 2020): profit $30,603 vs SPY $65,471; Sharpe 0.30 vs 0.46; worst drawdown −69.9% vs −55.2%.

How to read this

Dollars vs percent

S1 always trades $1,000 positions, while the SPY account compounds as it grows, so later-year dollar profits favor SPY. Year by year in percent, S1 beat SPY in 5 of 22 years, mostly years when the market fell or went sideways.

Hidden borrowing in 2008-09

Losses took the account down to $9,904 (2009-03-06), but the fixed-size rule kept opening $1,000 positions, so open positions reached 2.07x the account's value (2009-02-27). That implicit margin deepened the −70% drawdown. On average 65% of the account was invested.

Earnings data

Yahoo had earnings history for all 503 stocks; no year had more than 30% of candidates skipped for missing history, so no year is flagged.
